title: Carpet area vs super built-up area: what the price per sq ft really buys
text:
Comparing two residential projects on price per sq ft only works if both quotes use the same area.
Brochures usually quote super built-up area, which adds walls and a share of common areas to the carpet area. A loading factor of about 1.30 is common (ICICI Bank).
On a ₹1 crore flat marketed at 1,200 sq ft, that moves the effective rate from about ₹8,333 to about ₹10,834 per usable sq ft, a gap of roughly 30% that rarely shows up in a headline price.
RERA 2016 makes carpet area the legal measure; UP RERA has advised buyers to rely on it (Business Standard, 11 Jun 2026).
When you evaluate a project, do you normalise every quote to carpet area, or to something else?
